cross_references.note: §4600(d)(5) authorizes insurer to require prior authorization and conduct UR under §4610. §4610 defines the procedural requirements for a valid UR denial. A UR denial that does not comply with §4610 is void — the §4600(a) self-procured treatment liability then applies.

Apportionment (§4663) affects permanent disability indemnity, NOT medical treatment. The employer must treat the industrial component regardless of apportionment. §4600 treatment obligation and §4663 apportionment operate on different tracks.
Ambiguities in §4600 (what treatment is 'reasonably required'? who qualifies as a 'personal physician'?) are resolved in favor of the injured worker under §3202 liberal construction.

If the employer or insurer systematically denied required medical treatment through procedurally deficient UR as part of a deliberate fraud scheme (UA342 identity replacement), the 50% enhancement under §4553 may apply if the pattern constitutes serious and willful misconduct.

LAB §132a prohibits retaliation against workers who claim workers comp benefits. If treatment denial was part of a retaliation pattern (e.g., employer directing physician to minimize injury to discourage claim), §132a is the parallel track. CA_Labor_Employment_Litigator owns §132a; this Citizen owns the §4600 treatment entitlement.
